_note: T-TEST-15 fuzz regression corpus. A curated, PERSISTENT set of known-tricky / adversarial inputs, one per real past finding, replayed on every `node test/fuzz.selftest.mjs` run (the `corpus` phase, which runs FIRST and FAST, before the random fuzzer). Any crashing/edge input a fuzzer or audit ever found is pinned here so it becomes a fast, deterministic, permanent regression. Keep this SMALL and high-signal: curated regressions, not a random blob. To add a newly-discovered input see the 'add-procedure' block at the top of test/fuzz.selftest.mjs.

_schema.input: for onionToPubkey: the onion string. for verifyDirectory/verifyAnnounce: the object argument.
_schema.inputHttp: parseHttp only: { encoding: utf8|hex|base64, data } -> Buffer.
_schema.inputA/inputB: canonicalDirectoryBytes only: the two directory objects that must serialize identically.
_schema.pinnedSigner: verifyDirectory only (optional): the pinned-signer arg (hex string OR array).
_schema.expect.outcome: throw (call MUST throw = rejection) | decode (onionToPubkey returns 64-hex) | parse (parseHttp returns) | reject (returns {ok:false}, MUST NOT throw, MUST NOT be ok:true) | equal-bytes
_schema.expect.reason: reject: exact reason string.  expect.reasonPrefix: reject: reason startsWith.  expect.hex: decode: exact pubkey.  expect.equals: parse: deep-equal body.

entries.finding: loop-11: real total-ness bug in verifyDirectory -- a hostile directory carrying a NON-STRING `signer` threw on `.toLowerCase()` instead of returning ok:false. THE headline regression this corpus exists to pin.
loop-11 variant: an OBJECT `signer` must also be rejected as bad-signer-field, not throw. Guards the `typeof dir.signer !== 'string'` branch against the full grab-bag of non-string shapes.
total-ness sanity: a non-object (null) directory must reject no-directory, never throw.
total-ness sanity: a directory with no signature must reject unsigned before any crypto is attempted.

loop-13 (T-HARD-5 signer-rotation allowlist): the pinnedSigner arg may be an ARRAY. Non-string members must be dropped by normalizePinnedSigners so verifyDirectory stays total when the overlap set is fed junk. A garbage directory under such a set still rejects, never throws.

a string that is a well-formed 56-char v3 address (decodes to 35 bytes, version 0x03) but whose 2-byte checksum does not match SHA3-256(...). Must throw 'onion checksum mismatch' -- the address IS the key, so a forged onion cannot pass. (First char of the pinned test onion flipped u->a.)

loop-13 lineage (informational): a trailing-dot FQDN (`...onion.`) was a HIGH egress-policy bypass in the egress module. Here on onionToPubkey the trailing dot defeats the `/\.onion$/` strip, leaving a 62-char address that is correctly rejected as not-56-chars. Pinned so the onion decoder's trailing-dot handling never silently regresses.

loop-6 lineage (target-binding delimiter injection): a newline embedded in an onion address. The signal/announce encodings are newline-delimited, so a delimiter in a field must never survive into a decoded key. onionToPubkey rejects it (bad base32 length after the .onion strip).

happy-path anchor (testdata/vectors.json): the pinned valid v3 onion MUST decode to its pinned 32-byte ed25519 key. Guards against a change that rejects (or mis-decodes) real addresses while chasing the adversarial cases.
hostile / garbage bytes with no CRLFCRLF header terminator must throw 'no HTTP header terminator', not hang or index past the buffer. A lying bootnode cannot wedge the parser.

a well-formed HTTP response with a non-200 status must throw (never returns a parsed body from an error page). The 200-only contract keeps a hostile bootnode from smuggling an error body as directory data.
happy-path anchor: a proper 200 response with a JSON body must parse to that value. Guards against a change that hardens the parser into rejecting the real bootnode response shape.

loop-6 lineage: an announce whose onion field carries a newline delimiter. verifyAnnounce must stay TOTAL (async, returns {ok:false}) and reject at the onion decode (bad-onion:*), never throw an uncaught rejection.
total-ness sanity: a non-object (null) announce must resolve to reject no-announce, never an uncaught rejection.
total-ness sanity: an announce with an unknown version must reject bad-version:<v> up front, before any crypto or clock check.

signed-bytes invariant (fuzz property #5): the canonical serialization must NOT depend on key order or on unsigned extra fields, or a signature would be tied to JSON formatting. inputA and inputB are the same logical directory with shuffled key order + junk unsigned fields; they must produce byte-identical output.
